text_blocks.snippet: You can review official diagnostic guidelines provided by the American Diabetes Association which rely on specific blood tests.

list.snippet: A1C Test: This test shows your average blood sugar over the last two to three months. You do not need to fast. A result of 6.5% or higher means you have diabetes.
Fasting Blood Sugar Test: This test measures your blood sugar after you do not eat or drink anything except water for at least eight hours. A result of 126 mg/dL or higher means diabetes.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test: This two-hour test checks your blood sugar before and after you drink a special sweet liquid. A result of 200 mg/dL or higher means diabetes.
Random Blood Sugar Test: This test checks your blood sugar at any time. A result of 200 mg/dL or higher combined with symptoms like extreme thirst means diabetes.
Doctors usually repeat the abnormal test on a second day to confirm the diagnosis.
If you have clear symptoms and a high random blood sugar test, a second test may not be required.
Are you experiencing any symptoms like extra thirst or fatigue?
Do you have risk factors like a family history of diabetes?
